messages.content: My wife cannot get away early enough for either of those Friday flights. Please compare the last Friday departure with an early Saturday option. We still need to be in Edina before dinner Saturday, and we are still returning Monday.
I’ll reprice both for two travelers and adjust the hotel to two nights if you leave Saturday. Is the university-area hotel still the first choice, or should I compare both hotel locations again?
Keep the Graduate by Hilton. The ceremony being walkable matters more now. Compare complete totals, then we can book one.

The latest Friday nonstop is Delta departing Atlanta at 9:45 p.m. and arriving Minneapolis at 11:24 p.m. Two Main Cabin round trips, returning Monday at 4:35 p.m., total $1,006. Three nights at Graduate by Hilton, May 15-18, are now $642. With about $120 for rideshares, the estimated trip total is $1,768.

The early Saturday nonstop departs Atlanta at 7:05 a.m. and arrives at 8:43 a.m. The same Monday return brings two Main Cabin tickets to $948. Two hotel nights, May 16-18, total $428. Estimated rideshares remain about $120, for a trip total of $1,496. Both schedules get you to the 7:00 p.m. Saturday dinner in Edina; the Saturday option costs about $272 less.
How much practical risk is there with Saturday morning? I do not want the dinner to become a scramble if the flight runs late.

The scheduled arrival leaves more than ten hours before dinner. Allowing roughly 25 minutes to reach the hotel, bag storage if the room is not ready, and 30-40 minutes from the hotel to Edina later, you still have substantial room for a moderate delay. A cancellation or a delay of several hours would be the main exposure. The next Delta nonstop currently leaves at 9:20 a.m. and arrives at 10:58 a.m., which would still preserve the afternoon and dinner.
That backup makes Saturday reasonable. Are we comparing the same fare conditions, and can we get seats together?

Yes. Both quotes are Main Cabin, not Basic Economy, and permit advance seat selection. On the 7:05 a.m. outbound there are adjacent standard seats available in several rows. The 4:35 p.m. Monday return also has adjacent standard pairs. The fare is nonrefundable but can be changed, with any fare difference applying. The hotel’s two-night rate can be canceled without charge through 11:59 p.m. on May 14.
Use the Saturday itinerary. One king room for the two of us. Put us together on both flights, and use standard seats without an extra charge.

Available standard pairs are 18A-18B on Saturday and 21C-21D on Monday. The airfare is still $948 total for both passengers. The king room is $428 including taxes and mandatory fees. Shall I purchase the flights and reserve the room at those prices?
Before you do, confirm the timing for Saturday dinner and Sunday graduation from that hotel.

After the 8:43 a.m. arrival, plan to reach Graduate by Hilton around 9:30 a.m.; the hotel will store your bags until check-in. For Saturday’s 7:00 p.m. dinner in Edina, request a car around 5:45 p.m. to leave margin for weekend traffic. On Sunday, the ceremony begins at 2:00 p.m. and the venue is about a 12-minute walk away, so leaving the hotel at 1:15 p.m. remains comfortable.
Good. Book the Saturday flights with those seats and the king room for Saturday through Monday.

The reservations are confirmed. Delta confirmation V6N2KP covers two Main Cabin tickets: Atlanta to Minneapolis on Saturday, May 16, departing 7:05 a.m. and arriving 8:43 a.m., with seats 18A and 18B; Minneapolis to Atlanta on Monday, May 18, departing 4:35 p.m. and arriving 8:02 p.m., with seats 21C and 21D. The airfare charged is $948 total. Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis confirmation GH-593184 is for one king room for two adults, May 16-18, at $428 including taxes and mandatory fees. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. May 14, and morning bag storage is noted. With estimated rideshares of $120, the expected trip total is $1,496.
